Dividend appeal has increased sharply
Shareholder returns in focus following sell-off
We maintain our Buy rating on Samsung Electronics (SEC) but lower our target price to W370,000 (from W550,000). Just as the share price correction driven by lower NAND contract price forecasts had seemed to largely run its course, sentiment was further hit by concerns over China’s production of homegrown lithography equipment. That said, we believe the latter issue will have a limited impact on earnings through 2028. As such,  we left our earnings estimates unchanged but lowered our target multiple for the memory business.
Our target EV/EBITDA for the memory business is based on the current trading multiples of global peers and reflects our view that SEC’s valuation discount should eventually narrow. While the recent industry-wide sell-off appears excessive, we believe a reduction in our target price is nevertheless warranted. At the current share price, the stock is trading at a 2026F P/E of 4.5x and P/B of 1.9x―both exceptionally low in absolute terms.
For 2Q26, SEC reported preliminary revenue of W171tr (+28% QoQ) and operating profit of W89.4tr (+56% QoQ). Key points to watch during the Jul. 30 conference call include: 1) the terms of long-term agreements and the share of supply covered by them; 2) whether the memory supply shortage is expected to worsen in 2027 vs. 2026;  3) 2026F/2027F HBM shipment growth; and 4) whether the board approves an additional share buyback.
While memory ASPs are likely to continue rising next year, the pace of growth should inevitably moderate YoY. In our view, the focus should now shift to SEC’s ability to translate higher profitability into greater shareholder value. While investors await clearer evidence that stronger earnings are sustainable, we believe the company has an opportunity to bring its long-term strategy and investor expectations into closer alignment by delivering on shareholder returns and articulating a new strategic vision.
If SEC follows through on its plan to return 50% of cumulative 2024?26 free cash flow to shareholders, 2026 dividend yield could reach 6.7-9.3% for common shares and 9.3-13.0% for preferred shares. In addition, the company holds W18tr worth of treasury shares acquired in 1Q26 for employee compensation purposes (at purchase prices of W183,000?196,000). Given the scale of expected bonus payments, additional repurchases will likely be required. Of note, the current share price has fallen back toward the levels at which the company repurchased shares in 1Q26.
We expect 2027 to mark the first year of a meaningful step-up in shareholder returns. Over the past nine years, SEC has paid annual base dividends of approximately W10tr, or roughly W360 per share each quarter―equivalent to distributing 50% of an assumed three-year FCF of W60tr. Now, with cumulative free cash flow expected to exceed W800tr over 2027?29 even under conservative assumptions, the base dividend level is likely to rise substantially.
Despite the stock having fallen more than 50% from its peak, we see no indication of any meaningful deterioration in fundamentals. With the current share price implying a significantly higher dividend yield, we continue to recommend increasing exposure.
